PRECAUTIONS
Glasswares should be handled with care. A1 er adding conc. HN03, the solution should be boiled for few minutes for the complete oxidation of ferrous salt.
Ferrous salt solution should be freshly prepared otherwise Fe++ may get converted to Fe+++ due to aerial oxidation.
Fresh solution of potassium ferrocyanide should be used.

EXPERIMENT NO. 11
Object: TO DETERMINE THE SOLUBILITY OF THE GIVEN SALT
AT LABORATORY TEMPERATURE
APPARATUS REQUIRED
Desiccator
2. Porcelain basin
1. Beaker
Filter stand
5. Funnel
4. Air oven
8. Stand bath
7. Glass rod
CHEMICALS REQUIRED
Given soluble salt
THEORY
The solubility of a substance at a temperature is defined as the amount of the substance in gram that can be dissolved in 100 gram of water to form a saturated solution at that temperature.
Weight of solute Solubility = Weight of solvent x 100 Saturated solution Porcelain basin Sand Figure 6.3: Evaporation
PROCEDURE
Take about 20 ml of distilled water in a clean beaker.
Add small quantities of the salt a little at a time with constant stirring until a pinch of it is left undissolved.
Filter off the solution. The filtrate will be the saturated solution.
Weigh a small porcelain basin.
Miscellaneous Transfer all the solution into the porcelain basin and carefully weigh the basin having the solution.
Evaporate the solution to dryness over the sand bath stirring it with a glass rod to drive off the moisture.
Dry the basin having the solid residue in a air oven, cool it in a desiccator and weigh it again.
Repeat the process of heating, cooling and weighing till a constant weight is observed.
Note the laboratory temperature.
